dedupe_keys.name: truck traffic monitoring with satellite images object detection to aadtt

description: This model by Lynn Kaack, George Chen and Granger Morgan (a 2019 preprint for the ACM COMPASS conference) shows, as a proof of concept, that an object detection network can count trucks in satellite images and that the counts can predict average annual daily truck traffic. The motivation is that road freight produces a large and growing share of greenhouse gas emissions, while many low- and middle-income countries have little ground-based traffic monitoring or freight surveying. Coverage: the authors describe a complete pipeline from image to traffic estimate, test the uncertainty of the estimates, and discuss transfer to developing countries. Format and access: a 31-page preprint with 15 figures. Licence and cost: free to read on arXiv. Caveats: a proof of concept; single images capture only snapshots, so annual averages carry wide uncertainty, and the training imagery and code are not described in the abstract. The method can fill gaps in truck volume data used to calibrate freight network flow and emission models where counters are absent. It relates to the satellite heavy-duty truck detection framework and the Sentinel-2 vehicle speed dataset in the catalogue.
